purpose: Travoprost intracameral is used to lower pressure inside your eye, a condition called ocular hypertension, or to treat open-angle glaucoma. High eye pressure can damage your optic nerve and lead to vision loss if not treated. This tiny implant helps keep that pressure under control over a long period of time.
how_it_works: This medication is a tiny implant that your eye doctor places directly inside your eye during a short procedure. It slowly and steadily releases a medicine called travoprost over time, which helps fluid drain out of your eye more easily. By improving that drainage, the pressure inside your eye goes down and stays more stable.
common_side_effects: You may notice some eye redness, mild eye discomfort, or blurry vision, especially right after the implant is placed. Some people experience small floaters or see a shadow in their vision from the implant itself. Your iris (the colored part of your eye) may gradually become more brown over time with long-term use.
warnings: Tell your doctor about any eye infections, eye injuries, or recent eye surgeries before getting this implant. It should not be used if you have certain types of glaucoma where the eye's drainage angle is closed. Contact your doctor right away if you notice sudden vision changes, increasing eye pain, or signs of eye infection like increased redness or discharge.
typical_dosing: This is a one-time implant placed by your eye doctor directly into your eye in a clinical setting. It continuously releases medication for approximately 36 months (about 3 years). Your doctor will monitor you regularly and will discuss when the implant may need to be replaced or if a different treatment is needed.
